raw_response:
I am still doing the wheat-maize rotation on all 4.1 mu. At my age, with some people in the family working outside, I do not want to make big changes. What worked on my land before is still the main thing I trust. For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too much, because if wheat turns yellow in spring, the yield drops quickly and then it is hard to recover. But I also cannot spend too freely, so I will split it: some as base fertilizer, then add more at jointing if the stand looks good. Water costs money from the well, so I will irrigate at the key stages, not too many extra times unless the season is very dry. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is tight, so I will keep land preparation simple and plant quickly with hybrid seed like most people here. I usually give maize a decent first fertilizer and one more topdressing around the big flare stage. If rain is normal, one irrigation is enough; if it stays dry, I will add another. I am not chasing the highest yield, just a stable harvest without spending more cash than the small farm can carry.
